key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but accelerates degradation under thermal aging, with recombination losses spreading into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers distinguish interface passivation benefits from thermal-stability trade-offs in perovskite solar-cell stacks.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decay signatures using diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced fullerene-deposition-induced interfacial losses after treatment but faster degradation during aging, supported by simulations linking decay signatures to surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
watch_item: Depth assignments are model-supported rather than direct spatial measurements, and the abstract provides no quantitative device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
